From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Steve Rogers <srogers@acme.com>
Date: Sat, 16 Jun 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Weekly fleet / pipeline alignment — June sprint

Team — picking up from last week's handoff. We have three deals in close cadence with Acme that materially affect our dedicated pool usage for the next 6 weeks: the pilot (small), an expansion POC, and the enterprise commit. Quick asks for this morning's sync: 1) Marcus — can you confirm the effective burst slots we can provision without impacting current SLA-backed accounts? 2) Laura — I need a cost delta for the enterprise commit if we move from 80% shared to a 95% reserved slot profile (ballpark is fine). 3) Jordan — please confirm close windows for the three ACME opportunities so infra can prioritize.

Attached: capacity_snapshot_q2.csv (current pool by region), pricing_scenarios_v2.xlsx (baseline vs reserved). I also pasted the high-level ask below so we can be concrete in the call at 16:30 PT.

High-level: Acme pilot (50k tokens/day, 2–3 concurrent sessions) — target T-minus 2 weeks.
POC expansion (0.5–1M tokens/day, bursty inference) — decision window next Friday.
Enterprise commit (monthly reserved capacity ask) — target decision by 6/30; legal/procurement looped.

If we can get Marcus and Laura's quick notes in-thread before the call, I can update the action table and share with Acme.

— Grace
Senior Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: capacity_snapshot_q2.csv (CSV, 14KB); pricing_scenarios_v2.xlsx (XLSX, 72KB)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Steve Rogers <srogers@acme.com>
Date: Sat, 16 Jun 2028 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly fleet / pipeline alignment — June sprint

Thanks Grace — quick update from pipeline:
- Pilot: verbal go from Acme yesterday; legal loop in over next 5 business days. Target internal chore is spin up test pool by 6/28.
- POC expansion: demo scheduled 6/22; decision likely the following week (target 6/29).
- Enterprise commit: procurement wants finalized MOP and committed burst SLA; timeline still 6/30 but could slip.

I'll surface the exact usage patterns from the demo (expected concurrent sessions + token distributions) right after 6/22; that should let infra size burst profiles more accurately.

Jordan
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 16 Jun 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly fleet / pipeline alignment — June sprint

Grace / Jordan — quick infra read: based on the attached snapshot (thanks Grace), current spare capacity in us-west pool is ~22% with aggressive auto-burst headroom of ~150 concurrent RT sessions for short windows (under 90s median latency). If Acme's POC pushes sustained 0.5–1M tokens/day with long sequences, that will eat our effective KV-cache and force smaller batch sizes, increasing per-token runtime.

Conservative options we can action this week (low risk):
- Short-term: allocate 40 reserved slots to a dedicated pool for Acme pilot/POC for 2–3 weeks (fast, reversible).
- Mid-term: provision additional burst-capacity nodes (M60 class) to be available 6/25 — needs 48h infra prep and a confirmed start window.
- Fallback: route non-critical traffic to the hosted cheaper model variant during heavy windows.

Action blockers: exact session concurrency and average sequence length from Jordan (demo output), and finance sign-off for mid-term burst nodes. I attached an infra sizing sketch (embedded as rows in capacity_snapshot_q2.csv).

[Attachment: acme_multiproduct_mop.pdf (PDF, 220KB)]

— Marcus
Infrastructure Capacity — Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 16 Jun 2028 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly fleet / pipeline alignment — June sprint

Thanks — I ran the initial cost scenarios against the pricing_scenarios_v2.xlsx. Headline: moving from 80% shared to 95% reserved for the enterprise commit increases monthly unit cost by ~18% but reduces expected overage volatility (and therefore expected burst spend) by ~36% under our historical burst model. For the short-term 40-slot reservation Marcus suggested, estimated incremental run-rate is ~$14.5k/month (pro-rated if shorter window).

Two asks for procurement: 1) if Acme can commit to a minimum monthly token volume (we should aim for a conservative floor), we can move to a hybrid reserved model that reduces the 18% step to ~8% — Jordan, can you push for a 3-month floor? 2) If the enterprise contract is signed by 6/30, we need finance to approve the provisioning budget this week to avoid missing the 6/25 infra prep window.

DocuSign / procurement note: I uploaded the provisional pricing and redlines to the shared drive and started a DocuSign envelope for the pilot NDA and MOP. Link: https://docu.sign/company/ACME-commit-2028

— Laura
Director, Finance Operations
[Attachment: pricing_scenarios_v2.xlsx (XLSX, 72KB)]

Team / Acme — thanks for the quick turn. Summary & next steps captured below so we have a single source of truth before the demo on 6/22: 1) Action: Jordan to deliver demo telemetry by EOD 6/22 (concurrency + seq length + expected daily tokens). Owner: Jordan. 2) Action: Marcus to queue 40 reserved slots in us-west test pool (soft reserve) and prep burst nodes for 6/25 contingency. Owner: Marcus. 3) Action: Laura to finalize pro-rated cost for a 2-week pilot and the hybrid reserved scenario if Acme signs 3-month floor. Owner: Laura. 4) Action: Jordan to push procurement on the 3-month floor and accelerate DocuSign if possible. Owner: Jordan. 5) Decision point: if demo telemetry indicates sustained long sequences > 512 tokens with concurrency > 50, escalate to a permanent mid-term provisioning plan and lock budget (decision target 6/24).

I shared the updated action table on Drive (https://drive.company/shared/drive/fleet-runway/ACME-2028/plan.docx) and included the DocuSign link for Acme procurement. Steve / procurement@acme-corp.com — loop us if you need different artifacts or an extra technical call.

I'll run a 16:30 PT sync for 20 minutes (invite sent). Please join on time — we need infra to have the soft reserve queued before Monday morning.

— Grace
Senior Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
